title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Section β) 'Modules pour S ⊂ K ⊂ X' sets up a moduli or Teichmüller problem for conformal surfaces that carry an embedded combinatorial structure. The setting is the surgery operations of the preceding pages (removing or adding annuli, regluing along boundary circles).

The data are: a compact, oriented, (for simplicity) boundaryless surface X with a conformal structure; an embedded graph or 1-complex K ⊂ X; and a finite set S ⊂ K (vertices or marked points). Together, (X, K, S) is essentially a 'carte' (map) on a Riemann surface.

Rigidification. Fix a topological model S0 ⊂ K0 ⊂ X0. A rigidification of (S ⊂ K ⊂ X) is an isotopy class of homeomorphisms (X, K, S) → (X0, K0, S0), i.e. a Teichmüller marking. This kills automorphisms, since an automorphism isotopic to the identity is the identity. The exception is when X0 has components of genus 0 or 1 (with few marked points), where continuous automorphism groups survive. This is the standard Teichmüller-space philosophy, applied to triples rather than to pointed curves.

Normalization of edges. With K an arbitrary topological graph, the moduli of (X, K) up to conformal isomorphism is infinite-dimensional, because edges can be wiggled. A finite-dimensional 'bon espace de modules' therefore needs a rigid shape for the edges.
- First proposal: the edges of K are arcs of circles for the canonical projective connection. This is the CP^1-structure given by uniformization; circles make sense because Möbius maps preserve them.
- Grothendieck immediately notes the obstruction: the 'cartes cellulaires' (originally written 'holomorphes', then struck) do not necessarily satisfy this. These are the maps carrying their canonical conformal structure, obtained by giving each cell the structure of a disc.
- Alternative: impose conditions on the parametrizations of the cells by the disc. These are geodesic parametrizations, compatible with holomorphy of the cells up to the boundary (reading uncertain). Possibly add the condition that the vertices are equidistant on each boundary component of the disc, i.e. each face is a 'regular polygon'. This is exactly the normalization that yields the canonical conformal structure on a map described in the Esquisse d'un programme (Jan. 1984).
- He ends hoping that pieces made of discs 'avec facettes', carrying a metric of constant curvature (reading uncertain), give a workable model.

The page thus records the moment of choosing between two incompatible rigidifications of a map on a Riemann surface:
- edges geodesic or circular for the uniformizing projective structure;
- faces as regular polygons glued conformally (the dessin / Belyi canonical structure).
The note observes that the second does not imply the first.
errors: No outright error. The claim that rigidification kills automorphisms except for genus 0/1 components is the standard Teichmüller fact. It is slightly imprecise: with enough marked points in S, genus 0/1 components are also rigid, and Grothendieck's '.....' leaves this open.

The parenthetical 'l'équidistance ... du bord de la disque' and the closing sentence are fragmentary; the proposed normalization is not carried to a definition, so no finite-dimensionality claim is actually proved on this page.

ideas.what: Teichmüller-style rigidification of a triple (finite set ⊂ graph ⊂ surface) by an isotopy class of homeomorphisms to a fixed topological model; automorphisms eliminated except for genus 0,1 components
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller space of marked surfaces with embedded graph / marked ribbon-graph structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Teichmüller, Bers, Ahlfors (marking); combinatorial versions Harer, Penner, Kontsevich (1980s-90s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, rigidified moduli), Longue Marche (1981) in spirit

ideas.what: Requiring the edges of an embedded graph to be circular arcs for the canonical (uniformizing) projective structure, so as to get a finite-dimensional moduli space
ideas.modern_name: circle-arc / geodesic normalization of graphs on Riemann surfaces; CP^1-structures and circle geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: related ideas: Thurston circle packings (1985), Bowers-Stephenson conformal tilings (2000s)

ideas.what: Observation that cellular maps with their canonical conformal structure (cells as discs, equidistant vertices / regular polygons) do not have edges that are circles for the canonical projective connection
ideas.modern_name: incompatibility of the dessin (Belyi/equilateral) conformal structure with the uniformizing circle geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicitly in work on uniformizing dessins (Bowers-Stephenson 2004, Shabat-Voevodsky equilateral triangulations 1990)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme gives the canonical conformal structure on a map but, to my knowledge, not this remark

ideas.what: Normalizing cell parametrizations by requiring vertices equidistant on the boundary circle of each disc (regular-polygon faces)
ideas.modern_name: canonical conformal structure of a map (Grothendieck), equilateral triangulations

missed.claim: Grothendieck contrasts two rigidifications of maps on Riemann surfaces and notes they disagree: edges as circles for the canonical projective structure versus regular-polygon faces. He did not pursue a moduli space based on the circle-arc normalization. That alternative is a third 'canonical' geometry on dessins, in addition to the Belyi/equilateral one and to circle packings.
missed.quote: on pourrait v.ex. exiger que les arêtes de K soient des arcs de cercle pour la connexion projective canonique. Mais les "cartes cell." ne satisfont pas néc. à cette condition!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precursor of the question studied by Bowers-Stephenson of comparing discrete (circle-packing) and Belyi conformal structures on dessins. It shows Grothendieck was weighing projective-structure normalizations for moduli of maps around 1983-84. The interest is historical rather than mathematically new.

missed.claim: The notes treat moduli of conformal surfaces with embedded graphs together with surgery (cutting and gluing annuli and cylinders), in a 1983-84 manuscript. This anticipates the sewing/gluing formalism of conformal field theory (Segal, Vafa, Friedan-Shenker, ca. 1987) and of ribbon-graph decompositions of moduli space.
missed.quote: β) Modules pour S ⊂ K ⊂ X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is documentary evidence of Grothendieck's independent early work on surgery and moduli of conformal surfaces. On this page, however, it is only a setup.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a rough setup of a Teichmüller-type moduli problem for maps on Riemann surfaces. The one non-routine item is the explicit remark that the canonical cellular conformal structure is incompatible with requiring edges to be circles for the canonical projective connection. That remark, and the hesitation between normalizations, does not appear in the Esquisse as far as I know. It is mildly interesting historically but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'en a donc' should read 'on a donc'.
'On élimine ainsi les autres' is more likely 'On élimine ainsi les autos' (automorphismes).
'structure top.' probably 'structures top.' (for the triple S0 ⊂ K0 ⊂ X0).
'X compacte' is inserted above the line and 'compacte' is struck after X; the sentence reads 'On suppose X compacte, et pour simplifier que X sans bord (orientée)'.
'connexion[?] projective canonique' — 'connexion' is confirmed by context (canonical projective connection).
The final lines likely mention 'disques avec facettes' and a metric of constant curvature ('métrique ... à courbure constante'); the reading remains uncertain.
